title: Structs in Assembly
description:
## Structs
Assembly doesn't have structs like C. But structs are just data laid out at known offsets in memory.

A C struct like:
```c
struct Player {
    int health;    // offset 0, 4 bytes
    int armor;     // offset 4, 4 bytes
    int damage;    // offset 8, 4 bytes
};
```

In assembly is just:
```asm
section .data
    player:
        dd 100      ; health at [player + 0]
        dd 50       ; armor at [player + 4]
        dd 25       ; damage at [player + 8]
```

Access fields by base address + offset:
```asm
mov eax, [player]       ; health = 100
mov eax, [player + 4]   ; armor = 50
mov eax, [player + 8]   ; damage = 25
```

Or with a pointer in a register:
```asm
lea rdi, [player]
mov eax, [rdi]          ; health
mov eax, [rdi + 4]      ; armor
mov eax, [rdi + 8]      ; damage
```

You can even define constants for readability:
```asm
%define HEALTH 0
%define ARMOR  4
%define DAMAGE 8
mov eax, [rdi + HEALTH]
```


---
## Assignment:
LHINX stores process info as a struct: `pid` (4 bytes), `priority` (4 bytes), `memory` (4 bytes). Write a function `get_total_resources` that takes a pointer to a process struct in `rdi` and returns `priority + memory` in `rax`.
setupCode:
section .data
    pass_msg db "PASS", 10
    pass_len equ $ - pass_msg
    fail_msg db "FAIL", 10
    fail_len equ $ - fail_msg
    proc1:
        dd 1        ; pid
        dd 5        ; priority
        dd 512      ; memory
    proc2:
        dd 2        ; pid
        dd 10       ; priority
        dd 1024     ; memory

section .text
    global _start
starterCode:
get_total_resources:
    ; rdi = pointer to process struct
    ; return priority + memory in rax
    ret
runHarness:
_start:
    lea rdi, [proc1]
    call get_total_resources
    cmp rax, 517
    jne .fail
    lea rdi, [proc2]
    call get_total_resources
    cmp rax, 1034
    jne .fail
    mov rax, 1
    mov rdi, 1
    mov rsi, pass_msg
    mov rdx, pass_len
    syscall
    jmp .exit
.fail:
    mov rax, 1
    mov rdi, 1
    mov rsi, fail_msg
    mov rdx, fail_len
    syscall
.exit:
    mov rax, 60
    xor rdi, rdi
    syscall
hint: Priority is at offset 4 (skip pid). Memory is at offset 8. Use [rdi + 4] and [rdi + 8]. Use eax for 32-bit values since dd is 4 bytes.
